free_tier.stated: No. Sandbox is our no-commitment option. It has no subscription fee and includes no credits.
free_tier.notes: The free plan exists as a plan row and grants no volume. The same table lists Sandbox at $5.00/GB Tier 1 with extra credits at $500, so the free entry point is a zero-fee account that still bills every gigabyte.

per_object_cap.notes: A request through a mobile endpoint has no size ceiling published on either cited page; the product is sold by the gigabyte, so the unit that could carry a cap is volume, not object size.

retention.stated: not applicable to traffic: a session or an address, not stored bytes. The one 60-day clock in the product is on prepaid credits, which expire 60 days after being added.
retention.notes: days is null because the 60-day clock destroys a credit balance, not stored bytes. The clock is recorded in limits[] as retention-clamped, where it binds.

egress.terms: Traffic out is billed by the gigabyte and nothing is unmetered: Builder $200/month at $3.00/GB Tier 1, Team $500/month at $2.20/GB, Scale $1,500/month at $1.50/GB, Enterprise from $0.85/GB, and the free Sandbox at $5.00/GB because it includes no credits.
egress.free_allowance: none: Sandbox has no subscription fee and includes no credits

interface_detail: The mobile-proxy page states Control everything through an API - Access packages, sessions, and analytics, all through our API, and names integrations: Selenium, Puppeteer, Scrapy, and anything your team and agents run on. It also offers guardrails that limit protocols without naming them. Neither cited page states the proxy transport (HTTP versus SOCKS5), so the endpoint scheme is unrecorded here, not absent.
tooling: Any HTTP client that can be pointed at a proxy, which is what the page's own integration list names: Selenium, Puppeteer, Scrapy and anything else the client runs. The facts supply no CLI and no rclone backend, and a missing wrapper is a note about tooling rather than a reason to reject the provider.
chaining: The Worker's AI gateway sends its outbound fetches through a SOAX mobile endpoint, so the request leaves from a carrier address while the compute stays on Cloudflare; SOAX carries traffic only, and the mobile IP is the identity the target sees.

limits.value: zero free volume: Sandbox is our no-commitment option. It has no subscription fee and includes no credits.
traffic priced per gigabyte, stepping down with plan size: $3.00/GB Tier 1 on Builder, $2.20/GB on Team, $1.50/GB on Scale, from $0.85/GB on Enterprise, $5.00/GB Tier 1 on the free Sandbox
credits expire 60 days after being added

limits_note: Package guardrails the page names without a number: choose who can access packages, set traffic caps, limit protocols, whitelist or blacklist domains; targeting by country, region, city, ISP or ASN. Neither cited page publishes a per-request or per-IP ceiling, so the request-rate and per-ip-shaping kinds have no value to record rather than a value of none.
binding_note: Volume is purchasable at every size for a user needs, so no volume-quota bites at 45 GB a month; what fails first is the prepaid-credit clock, because credits die 60 days after they are added and capacity bought ahead of a workload cannot be banked, which is the retention-clamped kind applied to a credit balance rather than to stored bytes.

identity_cost.detail: A card, plus a business-use term. No usable volume is free, so any traffic is bought on a paid plan with a card: Sandbox has no subscription fee and includes no credits. The terms add: The Platform is designed primarily for business use (B2B). SOAX may decline access to the Platform for individuals acting in a personal or consumer capacity (B2C).

reliability_note: The page states a session can hold the same mobile IP across multiple requests or rotate on every request; the facts supply no suspension, throttle or data-loss report for the mobile network, and none was measured here.
confidence_note: Documented: every number the verdict rests on comes from the vendor's own pricing page, read on 2026-10-24. the record states the gap rather than upgrading the rung.

evidence.proved: The plan ladder and the free answer: Sandbox plan price $0 with $5.00/GB Tier 1 and no included credits; Builder $200/month at $3.00/GB; Team $500/month at $2.20/GB; Scale $1,500/month at $1.50/GB; Enterprise plan price $3,000/month listed with a rate from $0.85/GB; and the FAQ sentence No. Sandbox is our no-commitment option. It has no subscription fee and includes no credits.
Credits expire 60 days after being added, which is the clock this record binds on. The facts attribute this sentence to this page

The product is 3G/4G/5G mobile proxies billed per gigabyte with Builder shown at $3.00/GB Tier 1 and a $200/month plan price; sessions keep the same mobile IP through multiple requests or rotate on every request; an API covers packages, sessions and analytics; integrations named are Selenium, Puppeteer, Scrapy and anything else the client runs.

price_per_tb_month: USD 5.00 per GB Tier 1 on Sandbox, USD 3.00 on Builder, USD 2.20 on Team, USD 1.50 on Scale, from USD 0.85 on Enterprise; the vendor prices per GB and publishes no per-TB figure
notes: Four candidate routes to usable free mobile volume were considered and each was ruled out by the pricing page: (1) an included credit allowance, refuted by the FAQ answer quoted in free_tier; (2) a free trial on the mobile network, absent from both cited pages and not claimed in the facts; (3) a metered allowance billed only above a threshold, refuted by the absence of any included volume and by Sandbox carrying its own $5.00/GB Tier 1 rate; (4) free volume reached through the residential network instead, which neither page states and which this record therefore does not assert. The verdict is fails-quota rather than paid-only because a free plan does exist and grants no volume, so the failure is the quota at zero price, not the absence of an entry point. The facts' own note, that at 45 GB a month the entry tier is $135 a month, is the Tier 1 traffic cost (45 x $3.00) and sits below the $200 Builder subscription, so the record carries both numbers and does not reconcile them: the facts do not say how many gigabytes a credit buys and the page does not state it either. What would settle it is a signed-up account showing the credit balance, the first invoice, and whether a $135 purchase is possible at all. The Sandbox path was priced on the same page: $5.00/GB with no subscription fee, about $225 for 45 GB, more per gigabyte than Builder, so it does not change the verdict. Both cited pages were read once, on 2026-10-24, and no second read was made; no account, mobile session or counted gigabyte exists, so nothing here is at the measured rung. The B2B clause is quoted from the terms as the facts supply them, and no terms URL was supplied, so the record asserts none. Interface carries rest because that is what the two pages document; the assignment's socks5 and http-proxy tokens are not in scripts/dossier/schema.json's interface enum, so the proxy transport is described in interface_detail rather than written as a token the gate would reject. This record does not correct a record in another topic.
